stageA.product_summary: Front bumper module for an M1 passenger car. It combines a painted PP fascia, grille, EPP absorber, crossbeam with crash boxes and a lower stiffener. It also carries a licence-plate holder, a towing-eye cover and an optional EV charge-flap. Integrated electronics include camera, radar, LIDAR, PDC, pedestrian-impact and thermal sensors, a keyless-entry aerial, a wiring harness, decorative lighting and side signalling lamps (likely non-replaceable LEDs).

UN GTR 9.how_it_applies: GTR 9 is a whole-vehicle pedestrian-protection requirement for category 1-1 (≈M1) vehicles above 500 kg GVM. It does not approve components, but the front bumper is the structure assessed by the legform-to-bumper tests. The fascia, EPP absorber, bumper beam, lower stiffener and every attachment within the bumper test area together determine compliance with the FlexPLI limits (tibia bending moment, MCL elongation) or, for high bumpers, the upper legform limits (force sum, bending moment). The bumper's geometry (corners of bumper, bumper beam ends, lower and upper bumper reference lines, lower bumper height) defines the bumper test area and decides which legform test applies. The integrated pedestrian impact sensors point to a Deployable Pedestrian Protection System (active bonnet). If they are one, the bumper carries the DPPS sensing system and Annex 1 applies: detection within the detection test area, sensing time and total response time verification with the FlexPLI, and headform testing in deployed or undeployed state. Annex 2 also applies: HBM simulation to determine head impact time, against which the TRT is compared. The upper grille and fascia may also lie inside the headform test area (WAD ≥ 1000) on low-bonnet vehicles. The bumper supplier is affected through the vehicle front structure; the obligation sits with the vehicle manufacturer.

UN R10.how_it_applies: UN R10 does not regulate the bumper's mechanical parts, but the module carries several electrical/electronic sub-assemblies (ESAs, para 2.8): camera, radar, radar/LIDAR with heater, PDC sensor, pedestrian impact sensors, temperature/thermal sensor, decorative and signalling LED lighting, the keyless-entry aerial and the bumper wiring harness. Each ESA must meet the ESA emission limits (broadband 6.5/Annex 7, narrowband 6.6/Annex 8) and the transient emission limits (6.7/Annex 10). ESAs with immunity-related functions must also meet the immunity requirements (6.8/Annex 9, 6.9/Annex 10). These include the camera (indirect vision/ADAS), radars and LIDAR feeding braking and blind-spot functions, the pedestrian impact sensors feeding occupant/road-user protection, and the side signalling lamp if it is a direction indicator. These ESAs are approved as a component or separate technical unit, or validated within the M1 vehicle approval. Further conditions apply as follows. (1) An ESA that is, or is part of, a light source needs an R37/R99/R128 approval or a non-interchangeability report (4.2). (2) The ESA must carry the approval mark (5). (3) Conformity of production applies (9). (4) If the charge-port area includes the vehicle inlet or charging electronics rather than only a mechanical flap, the para 7 charging-mode ESA requirements also apply. Para 7 covers harmonics, flicker, conducted RF, burst, surge and immunity.

UN R127.how_it_applies: UN R127 is a whole-vehicle approval for pedestrian safety on M1 and N1 vehicles; there is no separate component approval. The product is the front bumper module of an M1 car, which is the core subject of the regulation. Under para. 2.11, 'Bumper' covers the front, lower, outer structure including all low-speed collision structures and any attachments. That takes in the fascia, absorber, lower stiffener, beam, grille, plate holder, covers, sensors and lamps. The module therefore has to be designed so the vehicle passes the bumper tests of para. 5.1 with Annex 5. The flexible lower legform test applies, or the upper legform test if the lower bumper reference line is high. The upper parts (grille, decorative light frame) may also contribute to the bonnet leading edge or front structure. The pedestrian impact sensors trigger an active pedestrian protection device, whose deployment is evaluated in the headform tests (para. 5.2 and Annex 5). The approval mark goes on the vehicle, not the bumper, so the approval marking provisions are not product obligations.

UN R137.how_it_applies: R137 is a whole-vehicle approval for M1 (≤3,500 kg) and N1, based on a 50 km/h full-width frontal impact against a rigid barrier. The bumper is not approved on its own. However, its crossbeam with crash boxes, EPP absorber and lower stiffener are part of the vehicle front structure, and that front structure is part of the vehicle-type definition (2.4). Through the crash pulse they directly influence whether the vehicle meets the dummy performance criteria and the post-crash requirements of para. 5. Any change to these parts can trigger re-test or extension. On EV variants, the charging-inlet flap in the fascia marks a vehicle inlet, which is part of the coupling system for charging the REESS. If that circuit is high voltage, the post-crash electrical-safety requirements of para. 5.2.8 and Annex 9 apply to it: IPXXB physical protection, isolation resistance and voltage/low-energy limits. These matter especially because the inlet sits in the front impact zone. The following parts carry no specific R137 obligations: the sensors, camera, PDC, aerial, decorative and signalling lamps, license plate holder and towing cover. They only need not compromise the frontal-impact result.

UN R148.how_it_applies: UN R148 type-approves light-signalling lamps as components. The bumper's '(Side) Lighting – signalling' segment strip on the lateral fascia is such a lamp: most likely a side marker lamp (SM1/SM2), but possibly a side or front direction indicator, front position lamp, parking lamp or DRL. That lamp, including any LED control gear declared part of it, needs an R148 approval and marking. Its installation on the M1 vehicle then falls under R48 (outside this regulation). The decorative grille-surround light guide is not a light-signalling function listed in R148, unless it also performs a signalling function. The other parts (sensors, absorber, stiffener, grille, plate holder, covers, EV flap) are outside R148. The front registration plate holder carries no lamp, and R148 covers only rear-registration plate lamps.

UN R152.how_it_applies: UN R152 is a vehicle-level 'if-fitted' regulation for the AEBS of M1/N1 vehicles; the bumper itself receives no approval or mark. It applies indirectly through the product's technology. The front bumper carries the forward-looking perception hardware (radar sensor, central radar/LIDAR with heating, camera) and the fascia, grille or radome areas the sensors look through. If these sensors feed the vehicle's AEBS, they form part of 'the System' (Annex 3) and are features significantly influencing AEBS performance (definition 2.4). The bumper module must therefore support: the general and specific performance requirements (5.1/5.2: warning and emergency braking against car, pedestrian and bicycle targets); self-check and failure detection, e.g. sensor blockage, heater or sensor faults (5.1, 5.5, 6.8); robustness (6.10); PTI verifiability (5.6); false-reaction strategies and safety-concept documentation (Annex 3 and its Appendices); and consistent production (8). Possible virtual testing using sensor models also applies (6.11/Annex 4). The structural, lighting, aerial, PDC, thermal, pedestrian-impact-sensor and charge-flap parts are not AEBS elements and are not addressed by R152.

UN R175.how_it_applies: UN R175 approves the whole M1 vehicle, including EVs with single-gear transmissions, for its ACPE system. It does not approve bumpers as separate components. It reaches this bumper only through its technology: the PDC (ultrasonic), radar, radar/LIDAR (heated) and camera sensors are the typical forward detection means an ACPE uses to detect an obstacle ahead of a stationary vehicle. If the vehicle's ACPE uses them, they become part of 'The System' under Annex 3. They must then support the ACPE performance tests against vehicle and wall-like targets (§5, §6), the continuous self-check and failure detection (§5.3), possible deactivation behaviour (§5.2) and PTI status checks (§5.5). The supplier must also provide documentation, schematics and the fault strategy for the vehicle manufacturer's safety concept (Annex 3). The fascia, grille, absorber, stiffener, plate holder, lighting, aerial and charge flap carry no R175 obligations. The bumper's mounting position, the radomes and any paint over the sensors can still affect detection performance, and changing them may require an extension of approval. Rearward ACPE is not covered by a front bumper.

UN R42.how_it_applies: UN R42 approves an M1 vehicle type for the behaviour of its front and rear protective devices in low-speed collisions. It is not a component approval: the bumper cannot be approved on its own. However, this front bumper module for M1 is the vehicle's front protective device. Its fascia, EPP absorber, crossbeam with crash boxes and lower stiffener therefore decide whether the vehicle passes. The tests are the Annex 3 front longitudinal and corner (60°) impacts with a pendulum or moving barrier, run at unladen and laden test weight. The bumper must provide protective elements at the reference height in both load states. After the tests, the vehicle's safety-related parts must still work properly. In this module that covers: the lamps (side signalling lamp and decorative lighting), the bonnet latch area, the cooling system behind the grille, and propulsion parts such as the EV charging inlet. Changes to the bumper's lines, dimensions or materials can create a new vehicle type or require an extension. Only the front protective device provisions are relevant; the rear protective device is outside this product.

UN R48.how_it_applies: UN R48 governs how lighting and light-signalling devices are installed on M1 vehicles, which covers their number, position, visibility, colour, switching and tell-tales. The bumper itself is not approved under R48, but it carries lamps: a side signalling lamp, decorative grille-surround lighting and, per the spec, 'functional' lighting. These lamps must be installable so the vehicle meets R48. The bumper geometry fixes key installation parameters: mounting height, distance from the outer edge, geometric visibility angles and apparent surface. Every installed lamp needs component approval under R148/R149/R150 and an R48-compliant installation. R48 does not recognise purely decorative exterior lighting as a lamp function. The grille surround light therefore has to be one of the listed functions (e.g. front position lamp or daytime running lamp), or be shown not to emit a light signal that conflicts with paras 5.x on colour, red-to-front and lamp list. The front camera may also act as the sensor for automatic main-beam or dipped-beam switching. The non-lighting parts are outside R48: absorber, stiffener, radars, PDC sensor, aerial, charge flap and plate holder (R48 has no front plate lamp).

UN R94.how_it_applies: UN R94 is a whole-vehicle frontal offset crash approval (56 km/h, 40% overlap deformable barrier) that applies to the M1 vehicle carrying this bumper. The bumper is never approved on its own. However, its structural parts lie in the vehicle's front structure forward of the driver's R point, which is a vehicle-type criterion (para. 2.6). These parts are the crossbeam with crash boxes, the EPP absorber, the lower stiffener and the fascia. They shape the crash pulse, energy absorption and intrusion, and so directly affect the para. 5.2 dummy injury criteria (Annex 4), intrusion, door and fuel-leakage results. Changing them can require extension or retesting of the vehicle approval. The bumper must therefore be designed and produced so the vehicle meets these requirements, with production consistent under para. 8. If the EV variant integrates a high-voltage charging inlet behind the bumper flap, that inlet is part of the coupling system for charging the REESS / high-voltage bus. It is then subject to the post-crash electrical safety checks: IPXXB protection, isolation resistance, low voltage or energy (Annex 11). The bumper's other electronics run at low voltage (camera, radars, PDC, impact and thermal sensors, lamps, aerial, harness). These and the styling features carry no R94 obligations, and the pedestrian impact sensors are not occupant airbags. Hydrogen safety (Annex 12) is not relevant to this product.
